Post cenam et collationẽ: Ost cenam sũe collationem cenobita fidelisũ siderium pro bono zelo et maxime animaruũ quo poteit feruore charitatis induat:et orans ad do- minum dicat. Oratio. Omnine deus amator maximus fidelũ animaruũ. qui,& salutẽ hominũ filiũ tuũ mori in crucis patibu- lo voluisti:da mihi p exemplũ eiũde filiũ tuũ in bono zelo semp,pficere:et pro salutẽ animaruũ nullos labores,nulla aduersa formidare:quatenus tuũ amoris incendio robo- ratus:cõtradicentibus tibi, oportune resistere audeam:

Lord Jesus Christ, king of heaven and earth, have mercy on me, for whom you died on the cross; and I humbly give thanks to you for your holy passion and most innocent death. O most loving Savior, what shall I render to you for all the things that you have rendered to me? Behold, I offer myself to you; I continually desire to dwell in your most holy wounds. I ask you, by the virtue of your most innocent death, have mercy on me as you know how; fasten my flesh with your fear, and restrain in me all disordered motions, so that, inflamed by the fervor of your most holy love, I may love you with a pure heart, confess you praiseworthy with my mouth, and follow you in deed, according to my strength, in humble conduct. I beseech you, most merciful Lord Jesus, by that anguish of your most holy heart which you endured on the cross, when your most holy soul departed from your body: have mercy on my soul at its departure.

The first hour after dinner.

The first hour after dinner. Unless you are occupied with higher exercises, for first obtaining knowledge of frailty, pray for the day in this or a similar manner.

Prayer

Almighty God, who out of your great goodness created me in the first parent from the mud of the earth, so that, mindful of my humble condition, I might glorify you, my creator, in true humility: grant me, I beseech you, truly to know my frailty in all things, so that, while I consider that I am both vile and almost nothing by my own merit, I may first deserve to please you by your gift. Through Christ.

The Second Hour.

At the second hour after midday let our cenobite bring back to memory the gravity of sins, both his own and those by which, especially while living in holy religion, he has sinned against the rule; and, turned toward the Lord, let him pray thus.

Prayer

Almighty everlasting God, who deigned, from your mercy alone, to make us wretched ones, dead in sins, alive by the incarnation and death of your only-begotten Son, our Jesus Christ: grant me, by the virtue of his most innocent passion, indulgence for all my sins and my own, so that henceforth I may deserve to serve you with a pure conscience. Through the same our Lord.

The Third Hour.

At the third hour after dinner let our faithful cenobite remember his vows and what he promised the Lord, and especially the renunciation of all property, namely in things, [unclear], and will; and, compunct in fervor of spirit, he shall pray thus to the Lord.

Prayer

Almighty and merciful God, who by kindly favor sanctify and receive the vows of your servants, offered to you from faithful devotion: grant me to render all that has been promised to you, and the virtue of humility, chastity, obedience, and poverty, with such purity of mind that I may deserve, with your mercy, to obtain your kingdom promised to the poor in spirit. Through our Lord.

After vespers:

After vespers let our good cenobite think that all visible things are vain; and, raised in mind to the love of invisible goods and to the Lord, let him cry out with as much devotion as he can.

Prayer.

Almighty everlasting God, who wished to lead us through the visible things which you created to knowledge and love of invisible things: grant me so to know the vanity of present things that I may deserve to think on the eternity of future things with a pure and [unclear] mind.

Another.

God, protector of those who hope in you, without whom nothing is strong, nothing holy: multiply your mercy upon us, so that, with you as ruler, with you as guide, we may so pass through temporal goods that we do not lose eternal goods.

Another prayer.

God, who have prepared invisible good things for those who love you: pour into our hearts the affection of your love, so that, loving you in all things and above all things, we may obtain your promises, which surpass every desire. Through the Lord.

After supper and collation:

After supper or collation let the most faithful cenobite put on desire for good zeal, and especially for souls, with what fervor of charity he can; and, praying to the Lord, let him say.

Prayer.

Lord God, greatest lover of faithful souls, who wished your Son to die on the gibbet of the cross for the salvation of men: grant me, by the example of the same your Son, always to make progress in good zeal, and to fear no labors, no adversities, for the salvation of souls, so that, strengthened by the fire of your love, I may dare to resist in due season those who contradict you;

et murum me pro domo tua viriliter opposam. Per eum dem dominu nostrum. Post completorium Ost completorii recollectis viribus suis cenon bita deuotus, cordis sui secretu solus introcet: omnes curas et sollicitudines nudi foras dere linquat: quatenus liber et absolutus ab omnibus cui dno iesu p desideri compunctionis mereatur colloqui: et p amoris incendi dulciter vniri. Revocatis itaç in sumo ma culpis diurnis ad memoriam examinis: sic oret ad dominum. Oratio. O Clementissime dne lesu christe: qui p nostra redema ptione subire mortem turpissimâ voluist: concede mihl obsecro p dolorem vulnerum tuo w ac p sanctissimi sanguinis tui effusionê. et innocentissime mortis tuae vir/ tutê omnii peccato p meoy ventâ: vt mûdata cõscientia tibi deinceps per desideriâ amouis iugiter adheream: in sancta religione quotidiie proficiam:et metues sanctissimi voluntati humiliter in omnibus submittam. Ad filium. Orpus et animâ meam tibi dne lesu christe hac nocte et omni tge cõmendo in virtute et vnione illius amoris qua d!lectâ genitricê tuâ virginem maria pendens in cruce discipulo cõmendasti: in qua me obsecro ab omnibus insldijs antiqui serpentiis custodias: carnis illicitos motus deprimas: turpia et mala somnia procul abigas: noctiumq phantasmata repellas: quate nus in tua pace securus dormia:et ad laudes tuas dispo sitis mihl houis hilariter cõsurgam. Amen. Ad patrem. Omine sancte pater omipotês eterne deus. qui nos ad gratiâ tuam in passione vnigeniti filiâ tuâ placide suscepisti: suscipe obsecro clementer omnia bona opaque te donate in hoc die operatus sum: verbis factis et cogitacõibus: in virtute et vnione illius charitatis et amoris, qua suscepisti eundẽ filiũ tuũ pendentẽ et moa rientẽ in cruce pro nobis. Ne tibi sancte pater in fide et vnione illius charitatis hac nocte et omni tempore cõmen do: qua filius tuus dũs nostre tibi moriturus iam spiritũ suum in cruce cõmendauit. Ad sanctamariam. Ancia et immaculata dei genitrix virgo maria: rogo te pamarã dulcissimi filij tuũ passionem et mortẽ: nó me alperneris miserũ peccatorẽ pter immũdam conscientiã meã: sed memento te matrem esse misericordie. et ora pro me deum quem genuisti: vt mihi peccata mea clementer indulgeat: amatorẽ me suum ferũ uentem efficiat: ab omnibus insidijs et malis hac nocte custodiat: et post mortem carnis animã meã ad vita eter nam perducat. and manfully set myself as a wall for your house. Through the same our Lord.

After Compline

After Compline, having gathered his powers, the devout cenobite should enter alone into the secret place of his heart; let him leave all cares and anxieties outside, bare of them, so that, free and released from all things, he may deserve to speak with the Lord Jesus through the desire of compunction, and sweetly to be united through the burning of love. Thus, having recalled the faults of the day in summary to the memory for examination, let him pray to the Lord as follows.

Prayer.

O most merciful Lord Jesus Christ, who for our redemption willed to undergo a most shameful death: grant me, I beseech you, through the pain of your wounds and through the shedding of your most holy blood, and through the power of your most innocent death, pardon for all my sins, so that with conscience cleansed I may hereafter cling to you continually through the desire of love; may make daily progress in holy religion; and may humbly submit myself in all things to your most holy will.

To the Son.

My body and my soul I commend to you, Lord Jesus Christ, this night and at every time, in the power and union of that love by which, hanging on the cross, you commended your beloved mother, the Virgin Mary, to the disciple. In that love, I beseech you, guard me from all the snares of the ancient serpent; suppress the unlawful motions of the flesh; drive far away foul and evil dreams; and repel the phantasms of the nights, so that I may sleep secure in your peace, and at the hours appointed for me may rise gladly to your praises. Amen.

To the Father.

Lord, holy Father, almighty, eternal God, who kindly received us into your grace in the passion of your only-begotten Son: receive, I beseech you, mercifully, all the good things, bestowed by you, that I have done on this day, in words, deeds, and thoughts, in the power and union of that charity and love by which you received the same your Son hanging and dying on the cross for us. And to you, holy Father, in the faith and union of that charity I commend myself this night and at every time, by which your Son, our Lord, when now about to die, commended his spirit to you on the cross.

To Saint Mary.

Holy and immaculate mother of God, Virgin Mary: I beg you, by the bitter passion and death of your sweetest Son, do not reject me, a wretched sinner, because of my unclean conscience, but remember that you are the mother of mercy; and pray for me to God, whom you bore, that he may mercifully forgive me my sins; make me his fervent lover; guard me this night from all snares and evils; and after the death of the flesh bring my soul to eternal life. To your protection, most blessed Virgin Mary, I commit myself this night and at every time, in the power and union of that commending by which your beloved Son, our Lord Jesus Christ, when now about to die on the cross, commended you to the beloved disciple.

On the Memory of the Lord’s Passion.

Since the passion of our Lord Jesus Christ is the gate of our salvation, through which the kingdom of heaven lies open to us, we ought, with whatever devotion we can, to exercise ourselves in it rather frequently, because we shall easily obtain the effect of our prayers if through the love of compassion we adore the Lord in the power of his wounds. Therefore, faithful cenobite, with what diligence I can, I warn, exhort, and ask you that, mindful of the benefits of God, you let no day at all pass in which you do not give thanks to your Savior for the bitterness of his

passionis et mortis agas. Et si prolixius quavis occasio ne nó puales: vno saltem verbo te gratũ exhibere redema ptori tuo nó recuses. Sic ipé dnis ielus reuelauit amato ribus suis quibus voluit: qm nihil gratius illi. nihilque vti lus nobis et passionis et mortis eius memoria cum gra taurũ actione recolere: et alios vt idem faciant admoine/ re. Accipe igitur verbũ abbreviatũ: ne te oratio prolixior faciat tediosum. Flexis in terrâ geni- bus simul complolis manibus dic. of your passion and death. And if, on any occasion, you cannot do so at greater length, at least do not refuse to show yourself grateful to your redeemer with a single word. Thus the Lord Jesus himself revealed to those lovers of his to whom he wished: that nothing is more pleasing to him, and nothing more useful to us, than to recall the memory of his passion and death with thanksgiving, and to admonish others to do the same. Receive, therefore, the abbreviated word, lest a longer prayer make you weary.

With knees bent on the ground and hands clasped together, say:

I give thanks to you, most sweet Lord Jesus, for all the wounds, pains, and injuries of your most innocent passion and death; I pray you, through that same death of yours, have mercy on me now and at the hour of my death.

To your most bitter passion and your most innocent death, Lord Jesus Christ, compassionating in spirit, I give thanks; I pray you, have mercy on me.

I praise, bless, and adore you, Lord Jesus Christ, king of heaven and earth, and I give thanks to you for your holy passion, by which you delivered me, a wretch, from perpetual death. I pray you, through the power of that same passion of yours: make me a participant for ever in your most innocent death.

Conclusion of this compendium, by Johannes Trithemius, abbot of Sponheim.

And, lest I be more prolix than is fitting, here I set an end to the compendium. For the venerable whole assembly of the abbots of our annual chapter commanded me in this place to avoid prolixity, lest lukewarm and worldly cloistered men make weariness their excuse. If the Lord Jesus, as I have always wished, gives us a life free from cares, I shall try to satisfy both my own intention and another’s request. For I have resolved, at the request of certain virgins dedicated to Christ, to hand down a rule by which any devout cenobite may exercise himself in the Lord’s passion against all temptations; and if he continues in it for a few months, exercising himself as he should, little by little he will fly sweetly from the humanity of Christ to his divinity by the ray of love. For to those who desire to arrive at the love of God, continual meditation on the Lord’s passion affords an easy approach, because while the mind, through compassion arising from the memory of the benefit of so great a lover, is pierced with compunction, it is lifted up, burning with tears and desire, to love. You, therefore, cloistered men dedicated to God, who have no leisure to attend to many things, receive these few things; in them, although there may not be a continuous blaze of love, it can nevertheless be renewed for those who weep.

Here ends the compendium of daily spiritual exercise, by Johannes Trithemius, abbot.
